clue.text: The cleaner is a graduate, hence the charm

parts.note: a char or charwoman is a cleaner, an old British term for a daily domestic help
taken as written
MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate's degree

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady with a degree wins everyone over with her personality.
explanation.walkthrough: A CHAR is a British cleaning woman; MA is a Master of Arts degree, standing for a graduate.
explanation.definitionFit: Charisma is a compelling personal magnetism, the kind of attractiveness that draws people in.

clue.text: Elementary transport, good in Paris

parts.note: a car is a means of transport
bon is the French word for good

explanation.surface: A remark about simple vehicles and French approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elementary' looks like it means simple, but it defines the answer as a chemical element.
explanation.definitionFit: Carbon is a chemical element, so it is literally elemental, a playful reading of the adjective.

clue.text: Dutch place offering service on the border

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held: 'Dutch place offering service on the border'. RN (service) + HEM (border) gives RNHEM; nothing in the clue supplies the initial A ('the' cannot), so a word looks misread or the clue is incomplete.
annotationWithheld.clue: Dutch place offering service on the border

clue.text: Lays into stylish parties

parts.note: in means fashionable or stylish, as in the in thing
sets are groups or parties of people

explanation.surface: Someone attacks fashionable social circles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lays into' suggests attacking, but here it means puts something inside, as an inset is set into a page.
explanation.definitionFit: To inset is to place or insert a piece within something larger, such as a small map set into a page.

clue.text: The way to restrict relaxation

parts.note: a mode is a way or manner of doing something
to ration is to restrict a supply

explanation.surface: Advice that cutting back is the route to calm.
explanation.definitionFit: Moderation is an easing or lessening of severity, a slackening of intensity.

clue.text: Made to step back-there's something afoot!

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: back tells us the word for a step is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a pace is a step

explanation.surface: Someone forced to retreat, then exclaiming that something is going on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns PACE into ECAP. 'Something afoot' normally means a plot brewing; here it is literally something on the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A toecap is the protective covering over the front of a shoe, quite literally worn on the foot.

clue.text: Total defeat for the Conservatives?

explanation.surface: A complete political rout for the Tories.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the answer into OUT and RIGHT: the political Right, the Conservatives, put out of office.
explanation.definitionFit: Outright means complete or utter; and the political Right being thrown out would be a Conservative defeat.

clue.text: Agree with top man in police on one point

parts.note: CO, commanding officer, is the man in charge
taken as written
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of the British police
E, east, is one of the compass points

explanation.surface: Siding with the chief officer of the police force on a single issue.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, Britain's plain-clothes detectives.
explanation.definitionFit: To coincide is to correspond or concur, as views that match exactly.

clue.text: Arguments a worker may well find attractive

parts.note: pleas are arguments put forward in a case
an ant is the classic worker in crosswords, from worker ants

explanation.surface: A labourer finds certain lines of reasoning appealing.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasant means agreeable or appealing, giving pleasure.

clue.text: Desiring change of place to get the best view

definitions.text: place to get the best view

indicators.note: a change of the letters of the word desiring signals they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Wanting to move seats for a better look at the action.
explanation.definitionFit: The ringside is the area beside a boxing ring or circus ring, giving spectators the closest view.

clue.text: A way to universal conflict

parts.note: ST, street, is a way
rife means widespread or universal

explanation.surface: A path leading to worldwide war.
explanation.definitionFit: Strife is bitter disagreement or fighting, a state of discord.

clue.text: Approach on the subject of true reform

parts.note: over can mean concerning, as in argue over money

indicators.note: to reform the word true is to remake it, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Raising the topic of genuine political change.
explanation.definitionFit: An overture is an opening move or approach made to someone, as in peace overtures.

clue.text: Sports equipment gives rise to endless debate

indicators.note: endless says the word for debate loses its final letter

parts.note: to discuss is to debate

explanation.surface: Gear used in athletics provokes arguments without end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' removes the last S from DISCUSS.
explanation.definitionFit: A discus is the heavy disc thrown in field athletics.

clue.text: Having to cope with the head's frame of mind

parts.note: to stand something is to cope with or bear it
a point is a headland, a head of land jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: A remark about having to deal with the school principal's mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' is not a person but a headland, which is also called a point.
explanation.definitionFit: A standpoint is a point of view, an attitude or perspective.

clue.text: Used the needle-so attached to it

definitions.text: Used the needle-so attached to it

parts.words: Used the needle-so attached to it
parts.note: describes something fixed to a garment by sewing it there with needle and thread

explanation.surface: A tailor sews a patch onto a jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stitched on has been sewn in place onto a fabric, joined with thread.

clue.text: Bringing up the rear nevertheless

explanation.surface: Coming last, but still in the race.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition reads the phrase literally: coming behind everyone, i.e. after all the others.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming behind everybody else is being last in line; the phrase also means in spite of everything, however.

clue.text: Calling on half-a dozen, chirp about it

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals

indicators.note: about tells us the word for chirp goes around the word it

parts.note: to sing is to chirp like a bird
taken as written

explanation.surface: Phoning six birds, which twitter about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal; 'chirp' is the birdsong verb, not a phone call, despite 'Calling' at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Visiting someone is paying them a call, going to see them.

clue.text: No rating should be without adequate training

indicators.note: should be signals the letters of no rating turned into something else

explanation.surface: Every sailor ought to be properly trained.
explanation.walkthrough: A rating is a sailor below officer rank, which makes the surface about the navy.
explanation.definitionFit: Being ignorant is lacking knowledge or education, untaught.

clue.text: The good earth, where people enjoy good times

parts.note: fair means good, as in fair weather
ground is earth or soil

explanation.surface: Fertile soil for some, a place of fun for others.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairground is an open space with rides and stalls where crowds go for amusement.

clue.text: Bill needs little money. Emphasise that

parts.note: AC, account, is a bill
a cent is a small coin

explanation.surface: An invoice requiring a small sum, with stress on the point.
explanation.definitionFit: To accent a word or feature is to stress or highlight it.

clue.text: Coin's a requirement where there's gaming

indicators.note: the word requirement signals that the letters must be re-sorted into another order

parts.note: coin's read as coin is, so all its letters including the S are used

explanation.surface: Money is what you need where gambling happens.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal is unusual: 'requirement' is read as the coin's letters being re-required, i.e. rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A casino is a building for gambling at tables and machines.

clue.text: Thinks fit Europeans sound

indicators.note: sound tells us the word for Europeans is heard spoken, not seen

parts.note: Danes are Europeans from Denmark

explanation.surface: Healthy Europeans judge something reasonable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like an adjective meaning healthy, but it is the homophone signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To deign is to condescend, to consider something worthy of one's attention.

clue.text: An American scientist has no team backing

indicators.note: backing says the words for no and team run in the opposite direction

parts.note: taken as written
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A US researcher without a supporting group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns the whole pair round. The scientist is Thomas Edison, the prolific American inventor.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Edison was the prolific US inventor of the light bulb and phonograph.

clue.text: In the future a wise man should assimilate page one

indicators.note: assimilate means take in, so the word for a wise man takes in other letters

parts.note: a sage is a wise man
an ace is one in cards and dice

explanation.surface: A forward-looking sage absorbs the first page.
explanation.walkthrough: 'should assimilate' is the container signal: the page-plus-one pair goes inside the wise man. ACE is a crossword standard for one.
explanation.definitionFit: The space age is an era of space travel, a phrase long used for a futuristic time.

clue.text: Beastly article-agitated mail will ensue!

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: agitated letters of mail are shaken up into a new order

explanation.surface: A nasty piece of writing, so angry post will follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Animal as an adjective means relating to beasts, brutish and physical.

clue.text: One joining a writer in a round and getting mellow

indicators.note: in puts one and a writer inside the round

parts.note: a ring is a round, circular shape
I is the Roman numeral for one
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: A person joining an author in a circle as they mellow with age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; 'joining' simply links the one and the writer side by side before they go into the round.
explanation.definitionFit: Ripening fruit grows mature and soft, becoming sweet with age.

clue.text: The musician's smooth

parts.note: the term a player reads on a score instructing notes to be played flowing and connected

explanation.definitionFit: Legato is the Italian performance direction for playing notes smoothly with no breaks between them.

clue.text: Leave in boy's headwear

parts.note: stet is the proofreader's mark meaning let it stand, leave it in
sons are boys; boy's read as boys

explanation.surface: Keeping a young lad's hat on.
explanation.walkthrough: STET is a printer's instruction to restore a deleted word.
explanation.definitionFit: Stetsons are wide-brimmed cowboy hats.
